examples.ko: 우리 팀은 이번 경기에서 새로운 전법을 썼어요.
examples.en: Our team used a new tactic in this game.

examples.ko: 상대 팀의 전법을 미리 알아 두는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's good to learn the other team's tactics in advance.

examples.ko: 그 감독은 수비 중심의 전법을 좋아해요.
examples.en: That coach likes defense-centered tactics.

examples.ko: 이 전법이 처음에는 아주 잘 통했어요.
examples.en: This tactic worked really well at first.

examples.ko: 게임에서 같은 전법으로만 이기려고 하면 금방 질려요.
examples.en: If you try to win a game with the same tactic only, you get sick of it quickly.

examples.ko: 전법은 좋았지만 선수들이 너무 지쳐 있었어요.
examples.en: The tactic was good, but the players were too tired.

explain: 스포츠, 게임, 바둑 이야기에서 '전법을 쓰다', '전법이 통하다'처럼 자주 말해요. 큰 계획을 말할 때는 '전략', 구체적인 방법을 말할 때는 '전술'을 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used in talk about sports, games and baduk, as in '전법을 쓰다' (use a tactic) and '전법이 통하다' (a tactic works). For a big plan people say '전략', and for concrete methods they may say '전술'.

examples.en: All the materials in the library have been digitized.

examples.ko: 병원 기록의 전산화는 몇 년 전에 끝났어요.
examples.en: The digitization of hospital records was finished a few years ago.
The company started digitizing its documents.
Thanks to digitization, it has become easy to find documents.

examples.ko: 시청은 민원 업무 전산화에 힘쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: The city hall is working hard on digitizing its civil service work.
Digitization is late, so we still accept applications on paper.

explain: '전산'은 회사나 관공서에서 '전산 시스템', '전산 오류'처럼 컴퓨터로 처리하는 일을 가리킬 때 많이 써요. 그래서 '전산화'는 종이로 하던 일을 컴퓨터로 옮기는 업무 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '전산' is used in offices and public institutions in phrases like '전산 시스템' (computer system) and '전산 오류' (system error). So '전산화' often comes up when talking about moving work from paper to computers.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 모든 고객 정보를 전산화했어요.
examples.en: Our company digitized all of its customer information.

examples.ko: 도서관에서 오래된 책 목록을 전산화하고 있어요.
examples.en: The library is digitizing its old book list.

examples.ko: 병원이 진료 기록을 전산화하면 훨씬 편해요.
examples.en: If a hospital digitizes its medical records, it's much more convenient.

examples.ko: 종이 장부를 전산화하려고 새 프로그램을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a new program to digitize the paper ledger.

examples.ko: 시청에서는 민원 서류를 먼저 전산화할 거예요.
examples.en: The city hall will digitize the civil service documents first.
Even small shops need to digitize their inventory.

explain: 종이나 사람 손으로 하던 일을 컴퓨터로 처리하게 바꾼다는 느낌이라 사무·행정 이야기에서 써요. 보통 자료, 기록, 업무 같은 말이 목적어로 오고, '전산화되다'라는 형태도 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It means changing work done on paper or by hand into computer processing, so it is used in office and administrative talk. Objects are usually things like data, records or tasks, and the form '전산화되다' (be digitized) also appears often.

examples.en: I learned how to make kimchi from my grandmother.
They say he was taught pottery skills by his master.
I came back to my hometown to take over the family business.
After being taught the secret recipe, I opened a restaurant.

examples.ko: 이 춤은 어떻게 전수받을 수 있어요?
examples.en: How can I learn this dance from a master?
I make a living with the skill I was taught by my father.

explain: 그냥 '배우다'보다 스승이나 윗사람에게서 기술이나 비법을 이어받는 느낌이 강해요. 가르쳐 주는 사람 쪽은 '전수하다'라고 해요. 보통 '~에게/께 ~을 전수받다'로 써요.
explain_en: Compared with plain '배우다', it feels like inheriting a skill or secret from a master or an elder. The person who teaches uses '전수하다'. The usual pattern is '~에게/께 ~을 전수받다'.

examples.en: Our team needs a tactical change.
The coach substituted a player for tactical reasons.

examples.ko: 전술적으로 보면 이 선택이 더 나아요.
examples.en: Tactically speaking, this choice is better.
This defeat is because of a tactical mistake.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 전술적 이해도가 아주 높아요.
examples.en: That player has a very high tactical understanding.
That player substitution was very tactical.

explain: 큰 방향을 정하는 '전략적'과 달리, '전술적'은 눈앞의 상황에서 쓰는 구체적인 방법에 관한 말이에요. 축구나 게임 이야기에서 '전술적인 변화', '전술적으로'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '전략적', which is about the big direction, '전술적' is about concrete methods used in the situation at hand. It is common in football and game talk, as in '전술적인 변화' and '전술적으로'.

examples.en: I studied with all my effort before the exam.
He is a player who gives his all for the team.
We decided to devote ourselves fully to the new business.

examples.ko: 전심전력해도 결과가 늘 좋은 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Even if you give it everything, the result isn't always good.
My parents devoted themselves fully to raising their children.
If you give it your all to the end, you have no regrets.

explain: '최선을 다하다'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 딱딱하고 글에 어울리는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '열심히 하다', '온 힘을 쏟다'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '최선을 다하다' (do one's best) but stiffer and more at home in writing. In everyday talk people more often say '열심히 하다' or '온 힘을 쏟다'.

examples.en: It was cold, so I turned on the heater.
I sat in front of the heater and warmed my hands.
It's dangerous to sleep with the heater on.
There is one small heater in the office.
Electric heaters tend to use a lot of electricity.
I always turn off the heater when I go out.

explain: 집에서 말할 때는 보통 '히터'나 '난로'라고 해요. '전열기'는 안내문이나 제품 설명 같은 글에서 볼 수 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: At home people usually say '히터' or '난로'. '전열기' is the word you may see in notices and product descriptions.

examples.en: I felt a strong bond with my comrades in the army.
They helped each other to the end out of comradeship.

examples.ko: 전우애는 힘든 시간을 함께 보내며 생겨요.
examples.en: Comradeship grows from spending hard times together.
The comradeship among the old army friends who met after a long time was warm.

examples.ko: 전우애 깊은 두 사람이 다시 만났어요.
examples.en: Two people with deep comradeship met again.

examples.ko: 전우애 덕분에 힘든 훈련도 견딜 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to our comradeship, I could endure even the hard training.

explain: '전우'는 같은 부대에서 함께 지낸 군 동료를 말하고, '전우애'는 그 사이에 생기는 깊은 정이에요. 일반 직장 동료 사이에는 '동료애'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '전우' means a fellow soldier from the same unit, and '전우애' is the deep bond between them. For ordinary coworkers, '동료애' sounds more natural.

examples.en: That painter is famous for avant-garde paintings.
It was an avant-garde design, so it felt strange at first.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 너무 전위적이라 이해하기 어려워요.
examples.en: This film is so avant-garde that it's hard to understand.
It's a theater company that isn't afraid of avant-garde attempts.
His music sounds avant-garde, but it's fun.

examples.ko: 전위적이어서 눈에 띄는 옷을 많이 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw many clothes that stood out for being avant-garde.

explain: 예술, 디자인, 패션에서 시대보다 앞서 새로운 시도를 하는 느낌일 때 써요. 외래어로는 '아방가르드'라고 하고, 반대되는 느낌은 '보수적'이에요.
explain_en: It is used in art, design and fashion for work that is ahead of its time and tries something new. The loanword is '아방가르드', and the opposite feel is '보수적' (conservative).

examples.en: You must turn on your headlights on a night road.
My headlight is broken, so I'm going to get it repaired.
When you enter a tunnel, the headlights turn on automatically.

examples.ko: 맞은편 차의 전조등 때문에 눈이 부셨어요.
examples.en: The headlights of the oncoming car dazzled me.
The headlight was dim, so I changed the bulb.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 낮에도 전조등을 켜는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: On rainy days it's good to turn on the headlights even in the daytime.

explain: 자동차 앞쪽에서 길을 비추는 불이고, 말할 때는 영어식으로 '헤드라이트'라고도 많이 해요. 차 뒤쪽의 불은 '후미등'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the light at the front of a car that lights the road, and in speech people also often say '헤드라이트' (headlight). The lights at the back of a car are called '후미등'.

examples.en: This piece is famous as the prelude of an opera.
The concert began with a short prelude.
That incident was the prelude to a big change.
The early heat is the prelude to a long summer.

examples.ko: 바흐의 전주곡 한 곡을 연습하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm practicing one of Bach's preludes.

examples.ko: 전주곡은 짧지만 분위기를 확 바꿔 줘요.
examples.en: The prelude is short, but it changes the mood a lot.

explain: 음악에서는 본 곡 앞에 나오는 곡을 말하고, 비슷한 말로 '서곡'이 있어요. 일상에서는 '앞으로 일어날 큰일의 시작을 알리는 것'이라는 비유로도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 이번 합의는 평화의 전주곡이 될 거예요.
phrases.en: This agreement will be the prelude to peace.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악이 아니라 어떤 큰일이 시작될 조짐이라는 뜻의 비유예요. 뉴스나 글에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a metaphor, not about music: a sign that something big is about to begin. You often see it in news and writing.

explain_en: In music it is a piece that comes before the main piece, and '서곡' is a similar word. In daily use it is often a metaphor for something that signals the start of a bigger event to come.

examples.en: Many people believe that God is almighty.
I'm not an all-knowing, all-powerful person.

examples.ko: 아무리 똑똑해도 사람이 전지전능할 수는 없어요.
examples.en: No matter how smart, a person can't be all-powerful.
When I was little, my parents seemed all-powerful.

examples.ko: 그 소설 속 주인공은 전지전능해서 재미가 없어요.
examples.en: The hero of that novel is all-powerful, so it's not fun.
We're not all-powerful, so it's okay to make mistakes sometimes.

explain: 주로 신이나 절대적인 존재를 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 사람에게 쓰면 '뭐든 다 아는 척한다'는 과장이나 농담처럼 들릴 수 있어요. 보통 '전지전능한 신'처럼 앞에서 꾸며 줘요.
explain_en: It is mainly used for God or an absolute being. Used for a person, it can sound like exaggeration or a joke about acting like you know everything. It is usually used before a noun, as in '전지전능한 신'.

examples.en: This match is a warm-up skirmish before the final.

examples.ko: 오늘 회의는 내일 협상의 전초전이 될 거예요.
examples.en: Today's meeting will be a preliminary round for tomorrow's negotiation.
The small quarrel was the opening skirmish of a big fight.

examples.ko: 두 후보는 이번 토론을 전초전으로 생각해요.
examples.en: The two candidates see this debate as a preliminary battle.
The pre-election skirmishing has already started heatedly.
That game was nothing more than a preliminary skirmish.

explain: 본격적인 승부가 시작되기 전에 가볍게 먼저 부딪치는 싸움이나 경기를 말해요. 스포츠, 정치, 협상 이야기에서 비유로 많이 쓰고 '~의 전초전'의 형태로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to a lighter clash or game before the real contest begins. It is often used figuratively in sports, politics and negotiations, and commonly appears in the form '~의 전초전' (the preliminary round of ~).

examples.ko: 이 한옥은 전통미가 잘 살아 있어요.
examples.en: This hanok keeps its traditional beauty well.
I felt a uniquely Korean traditional beauty in the pottery.
It's a building with both traditional and modern beauty.
Traditional beauty can also come from simple lines.
I drank tea at a teahouse full of traditional charm.
This hanbok has comfort as well as traditional beauty.

explain: '-미'는 아름다움을 뜻하는 말로, '자연미', '곡선미'처럼 여러 말에 붙어요. '전통미'는 한옥, 한복, 도자기처럼 전통적인 것에서 느끼는 멋을 말할 때 써요. 짝이 되는 말은 '현대미'예요.
explain_en: '-미' means beauty and attaches to many words, like '자연미' (natural beauty) and '곡선미' (beauty of curves). '전통미' is used for the charm you feel in traditional things like hanok, hanbok and pottery. Its counterpart is '현대미'.

examples.en: That person's way of speaking is a bit combative.
The meeting went on in a combative atmosphere.
He works fiercely every day.
You don't have to be so combative.
I prepared with a fighting spirit and passed.
I like a gentle explanation that isn't aggressive.

explain: 실제 전투가 아니라 사람의 태도나 말투가 공격적이거나 의욕이 넘칠 때 써요. 문맥에 따라 '공격적이라 부담스럽다'는 뜻일 수도 있고 '열정적으로 달려든다'는 뜻일 수도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used not for actual battles but for a person's attitude or tone when it is aggressive or full of drive. Depending on context, it can mean 'so aggressive it's off-putting' or 'throwing oneself in with passion'.

examples.en: Because of the exam, I cut off all contact with my friends.

examples.ko: 그는 슬퍼서 식음을 전폐하고 누워 있어요.
examples.en: He is so sad that he has stopped eating and drinking and is lying down.
I decided to stop going to gatherings altogether for a while.
I dropped even the housework and just slept for a few days.
If you stop practicing completely, your skills drop quickly.
After giving up social media entirely, I felt more at ease.

explain: 어떤 일을 완전히 그만두거나 아예 하지 않는다는 느낌이라 조금 딱딱해요. 대화에서는 '끊다', '다 접다'라고 더 자주 말해요. 보통 '~을 전폐하고 ~에 매달리다'처럼 쓰여요.

phrases.en: Sunk in grief, he stopped eating and drinking altogether.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹고 마시는 것도 하지 않을 만큼 큰 슬픔이나 걱정에 빠졌을 때 쓰는 굳은 표현이에요. 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fixed expression for being so deep in grief or worry that one stops even eating and drinking. It is common in writing and news.

explain_en: It means giving something up completely or not doing it at all, and it sounds a bit stiff. In conversation people more often say '끊다' or '다 접다'. It is often used like '~을 전폐하고 ~에 매달리다' (drop ~ entirely and cling to ~).

examples.en: Citizens fully supported the new policy.

examples.ko: 부모님이 제 꿈을 전폭적인 지원으로 도와주셨어요.
examples.en: My parents helped my dream with full support.
I got full support, so I felt energized.
It isn't total, but many people agree.

examples.ko: 회사의 전폭적인 지원 속에서 연구를 끝냈어요.
examples.en: I finished the research with the company's full backing.
They say the government will help in full.

explain: '지지', '지원', '신뢰', '협조'처럼 마음이나 도움을 주는 말과 잘 어울려요. '전폭적으로 지지하다', '전폭적인 지원'처럼 쓰고, 반대 느낌은 '부분적'이에요.
explain_en: It pairs well with words about backing or help, such as '지지', '지원', '신뢰' and '협조'. It is used as in '전폭적으로 지지하다' and '전폭적인 지원', and the opposite feel is '부분적' (partial).

examples.en: Employees are having a hard time because of the CEO's abuse of power.

examples.ko: 회사 안에서 전횡을 일삼는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: There is someone in the company who keeps abusing power.
To stop the abuse of power by those in authority, oversight is needed.

examples.ko: 그 단체는 한 사람의 전횡으로 무너졌어요.
examples.en: That organization collapsed because of one person's high-handedness.

examples.ko: 이런 전횡은 더 이상 참을 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't put up with this kind of high-handedness anymore.
When the abuse continued, everyone protested.

explain: 권력을 가진 사람이 다른 사람의 의견을 무시하고 제멋대로 일을 처리하는 것을 비판할 때 써요. 뉴스나 글에서 '전횡을 일삼다'의 형태로 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used to criticize someone with power who ignores others' opinions and does as they please. In news and writing it often appears as '전횡을 일삼다' (habitually abuse power).

examples.en: Mom is pounding garlic in the mortar.

examples.ko: 깨를 절구로 찧으면 향이 더 좋아요.
examples.en: If you grind sesame in a mortar, the aroma is better.

examples.ko: 시골집 마당에 오래된 절구가 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old mortar in the yard of the country house.

examples.ko: 요즘은 절구 대신 믹서를 쓰는 집이 많아요.
examples.en: These days many homes use a blender instead of a mortar.
Grandmother washed the mortar clean and let it dry.

examples.ko: 이 절구는 돌로 만들어서 아주 무거워요.
examples.en: This mortar is made of stone, so it's very heavy.

explain: 곡식이나 마늘, 깨 등을 안에 넣고 찧는 통 모양 도구예요. 그 안에서 내리쳐 찧는 막대는 '절굿공이'라고 해요. 요즘 집에서는 믹서나 작은 분쇄기를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is a bowl-shaped tool in which you pound grain, garlic, sesame and so on. The pestle you pound with is called '절굿공이'. These days many homes use a blender or small grinder instead.

examples.en: At the factory, they cut steel plates with a cutter.
The cutter broke down, so the work stopped.

examples.ko: 절단기를 쓸 때는 장갑을 꼭 껴야 해요.
examples.en: You must wear gloves when using the cutting machine.

examples.ko: 이 절단기는 종이를 한 번에 열 장 잘라요.
examples.en: This cutter cuts ten sheets of paper at once.
The price of the new cutter is higher than I thought.
Be careful not to get your hand caught in the cutter.

explain: 종이, 철, 파이프 같은 것을 자르는 기계나 도구를 말해요. 책상에서 쓰는 작은 칼은 보통 '커터칼'이라고 하고, '절단기'는 더 크고 힘이 센 기계를 떠올려요.
explain_en: It refers to a machine or tool that cuts things like paper, metal or pipes. The small knife used at a desk is usually called a '커터칼', while '절단기' brings to mind a bigger, more powerful machine.

examples.en: They say the police caught the thief.

examples.ko: 가게 앞 CCTV에 절도범의 모습이 찍혔어요.
examples.en: The thief was caught on the CCTV in front of the shop.
They say the thief came in through the window.
That thief turned himself in a few days later.

examples.ko: 동네에서 가방을 도둑맞은 사람들이 절도범에게 화가 났어요.
examples.en: People in the neighborhood whose bags were stolen were angry at the thief.
The neighbors told us to watch out for thieves.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 보통 '도둑'이라고 하고, '절도범'은 뉴스나 경찰 이야기에서 더 자주 들려요. 몰래 물건을 훔친 사람을 가리키고, 사람을 위협해서 빼앗는 '강도'와는 달라요.
explain_en: In everyday talk people usually say '도둑', and '절도범' is heard more in news and police stories. It refers to someone who secretly steals things, which differs from '강도', who takes things by threatening people.

examples.en: I hurt my ankle, so I keep limping.
He came walking, limping on one leg.
Why are you walking with such a limp?
The puppy was limping on its front paw, so we went to the vet.
My friend who used to limp walks well now.

examples.ko: 신발이 안 맞아서 절뚝댈 정도로 아팠어요.
examples.en: The shoes didn't fit, and it hurt so much I almost limped.

explain: 다리가 불편해서 몸이 한쪽으로 기우뚱하며 걷는 모습이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '절뚝거리다'도 쓰고, 센 느낌은 '쩔뚝대다'예요. '다리를 절다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It describes walking with the body tilting to one side because of a bad leg. '절뚝거리다' is also used for the same meaning, and '쩔뚝대다' is a stronger-sounding version. People also say '다리를 절다'.

examples.en: He limped to the bus and got on.
The puppy came limping, and my heart ached.
I climbed the stairs limping on my injured leg.
The sight of him limping along was pitiful.
Since falling, the child runs with a limp.
Grandfather smiled even while limping along.

explain: '걷다', '가다', '오다', '뛰다' 같은 움직임 말 앞에서 한쪽 다리가 불편한 걸음걸이를 보여 줘요. 더 센 느낌으로 '쩔뚝쩔뚝'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It goes before movement words like '걷다', '가다', '오다' and '뛰다' to show a gait with one bad leg. A stronger-sounding version is '쩔뚝쩔뚝'.
